findings.title: Exposed .git directory
findings.description: The .git directory is web-accessible, which can allow an attacker to reconstruct source code, commit history, and any secrets ever committed.
findings.recommendation: Block web access to .git/ (e.g. deny in the web server config) or remove it from the deployed document root entirely.

findings.title: TLS certificate expires soon
findings.recommendation: Renew the certificate before it expires to avoid an outage.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy (CSP)
findings.description: No CSP header was found. CSP is a key mitigation against cross-site scripting and data-injection attacks.
findings.recommendation: Define a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, starting from default-src 'self' and widening only as needed.

findings.title: Cookie 'session' missing SameSite attribute
findings.description: Without SameSite, this cookie may be sent on cross-site requests, weakening CSRF defenses.
findings.recommendation: Set SameSite=Lax (or Strict) unless cross-site delivery is explicitly required.

findings.title: Server software disclosed via Server
findings.description: The 'Server' header reveals server/framework details ('nginx/1.18.0'), which helps attackers target known vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Suppress or genericize the 'Server' header at the reverse proxy / server configuration level.
